newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Air Afrique board to examine accounts Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Air Afrique board to examine accounts Thursday.

text.p: The board of struggling multi-national carrier Air Afrique meets in Ivory Coast's commercial capital on Thursday to examine the accounts for 1995-96, a spokesman said.
"It will be an ordinary meeting to approve the accounts," Marc Amoussou told Reuters on Tuesday.
He said the meeting had been planned for June but was put back in the light of an emergency meeting in July to discuss debt payments.
The airline, set up in 1961 by 11 countries following independence from France, has debts approaching $400 million but owner countries see it as a symbol of pan-African cooperation.
The main problem facing it has been its inability to earn enough money to make interest payments on the debt dating back to the purchase of four Airbus A-310 airliners.
The debt doubled with the 1994 devaluation of the CFA franc used in much of French-speaking Africa. Air Afrique's 1995 losses approached $20 million.
The airline serves West and Central Africa and has longer-haul flights to Europe, the United States and South Africa. Proposed solutions have included the sale and lease back of the planes.

Benin, Burkina Faso, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, Ivory Coast, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Senegal and Togo own the airline along with French national carrier Air France and a number of private shareholders.
